raw_response:
I’m planting all 10.1 mu to cotton again this year. I’ve done cotton for years, and on my land it’s what I know best. Wheat-maize can spread risk, but with some people in my family working off-farm, I don’t want the tight timing and extra labor. Cotton takes more watching through the season, but the work is more spread out, and with the well I can manage if spring is dry. The extension fellow talks about more exact fertilizer rates, but I still mostly go by what I saw before: if I’m too stingy, the cotton stays weak and doesn’t set bolls well; if I push too much fertilizer, it grows too lush and costs me more cash. So I’ll stay near what worked for me before, maybe a little careful on spending. I’ll use improved seed from the local dealer, put most fertilizer down before planting, then add a smaller topdressing once the plants are growing steadily. Water is expensive to pump, so I won’t irrigate too often, only at the key times. For pests, cotton can’t be ignored, so I’ll keep herbicide early and insecticide ready if aphids or bollworm show up.
